items.review_rationale: Read prime ideal of commutative unital ring as proper ideal satisfying ab in P implies a or b in P, distinguishing prime property from maximality.

references.context: Ring with commutative multiplication and specified identity.
For all ring elements a,b, ab∈P entails a∈P or b∈P.

references.phrase: prime ideal need not be maximal
references.disposition: Maximal ideals are prime for commutative unital rings, but not all prime ideals are maximal.

items.review_rationale: Read field as nonzero commutative unital ring where every nonzero element has multiplicative inverse, tracking 0≠1 and unit condition.

references.context: Multiplication commutative, with specified two-sided multiplicative identity.
Additive zero differs from multiplicative unit, excluding zero ring.
For each nonzero a exists b with ab=ba=1.

references.phrase: field requires all nonzero elements invertible
references.disposition: Integral domains need not be fields; no alternative division-ring noncommutative context is assumed.

items.review_rationale: Read indexed family of arrows to common category object U, retaining potentially empty index set, distinct source objects and duplicate arrow occurrences.

references.context: Indexing set may be empty and need not inject into arrow set.
For each index i, independently specified domain object U_i and morphism to fixed target U.

references.disposition: Equal underlying arrows with different index labels count as separate occurrences.

items.review_rationale: Read Grothendieck site via small category with indexed covering families satisfying isomorphism, composition/refinement and base-change axioms.

references.context: Specified class of indexed families of arrows with common target deemed covering.
Each one-arrow family consisting of categorical isomorphism must be a covering.
Covering families remain covering under composites with covering families of each member's domain.
Pullback of covering family along any arrow remains covering when necessary fiber products exist.

references.disposition: Equivalent Grothendieck topology via covering sieves is a distinct presentation.
